# Local draft characterization and initial contract

`local-draft-cases.json` contains 30 observations from the real pre-port JS exports. The fixture records the remote snapshot commit and SHA-256 of every relevant source file and the generator. Its MIME/read/store/index replies are scripted dependency inputs. It proves JS mapping, call ordering, exact descriptor/byte forwarding and session transformation only. It does not prove Rust MIME semantics, durable files/indexes, App hydration order, component debounce, or cross-webview UID allocation.

Generate only in an authorized disposable remote job with `MAILVAULT_GENERATE_DRAFT_FIXTURE=1 npx vitest run src-core/tests/fixtures/gen/local-draft-cases.test.js`. The unique stdout base64 markers transfer exact generated bytes. Ordinary runs compare observations without writing. Do not regenerate from a native facade after cutover; archive this generator then, following the bulk oracle precedent.

The unsafe named cases are evidence of old defects, not port requirements. The staged shape uses actual old `openLocalDraft` source-only admission; an actual native `compose.stage` refusal test belongs to the lifecycle slice. Empty provided content currently throws. Delete IO failure currently hides the row and resolves. Recipient row splitting currently splits a quoted display-name comma; MIME envelope parsing remains the reopening authority.

`composeDraftRevision.test.jsx` mounts actual ComposeModal with real quote/text helpers and fake time. IO adapters and the rich editor DOM are stubbed, retaining actual component scheduling, save chain, identity refs and snapshot publication. Initial contracts cover all-clear, same-length quote, equal-size changed attachment bytes, account change during deferred folder lookup, destination failure and handoff wait. These are component orchestration assertions, not a durable filesystem claim. Native race/failure/restart and stale-reply adoption with stable native revisions are introduced with their corresponding lifecycle/UI slices.

## Narrow proposed wire contract

`drafts.save` takes `{draftId, revision, accountId, fromAddress, displayName, snapshot, snippet, previousIdentity?}`. `snapshot` requires string `to,cc,bcc,subject,html,text,inReplyTo,references` and ordered `attachments:[]`. Each attachment has `filename,contentType`, optional `cid`, and either base64 `content` (including `""`) or `source:{accountId,mailbox,uid,attachmentIndex}`. `encoding`, if present, must be `base64`; the UI adapter explicitly converts `_source` to `source`. Missing complete fields produce JSON-RPC INVALID_PARAMS before account/storage work. Explicit empty values are valid edits.

The reply is `{draftId,revision,accountId,mailbox,uid,entry,disposition:"saved"|"unchanged"|"superseded"}`. Fingerprints include resolved bytes and all complete fields; generated MIME randomness is excluded. Equal revision/different fingerprint conflicts. Stable draft id and issued/accepted revisions travel in the existing UI session. Native account and custody folder reads are authoritative; no credentials, digest or receipt in an RPC grants ownership.

`drafts.list` takes `{accountId?,identity?:{accountId,mailbox,uid},includeContent?:false}` and returns `{drafts:[{draftId,revision,accountId,mailbox,uid,entry}]}`. One exact identity with `includeContent:true` returns `{drafts:[{draftId,revision,accountId,mailbox,uid,entry,eml}],missingBody:false}` or `{drafts:[],missingBody:true}`. Content requests without one exact identity are invalid. Legacy admission requires real bytes, archived user-draft custody and exclusion of Scheduled/staged-send ownership; one legacy tuple maps to one stable id. Metadata listing never fetches all bodies.

`drafts.discard` takes `{draftId,revision?}`; exact legacy tuple compatibility must first establish draft-purpose ownership. Reply `{draftId,discarded:true,cleanup:"complete"|"pending"}` separates durable terminal acceptance from physical cleanup. The UI retains pending identity and reports cleanup failure; post-send/schedule cleanup cannot convert accepted delivery/scheduling into Retry.

## Proposed app.db shape

At this base app.db schema is 10. Add the next ordered migration, normally 11, preserving schema 10 and legacy NULL purge proof semantics. A small `local_drafts` table has primary `draft_id`, accepted revision/fingerprint, terminal flag, exact current identity/proof, an array of ALL pending exact cleanup locations/native proofs, and versioned pending intent. Each cleanup item is removed only after its own exact retirement or reconciliation, including repeated failed account moves. No later move may overwrite an older pending item. Unique adopted physical ownership prevents two ids adopting one legacy tuple. Exact proof is native account/mailbox/UID, normalized Message-ID and raw SHA-256, with narrow draft purpose validated separately. An intent names prepared bytes retained in existing vault/message-store storage plus the proposed complete row/location and preparation fingerprint; bodies and attachments never live in app.db. Pending equal revision reconciles, rather than returning unchanged. Destination verifies before metadata switches and source retires. No second journal, account service, settings store or new shared locking layer is proposed.
